name: Cadillac Mountain Sunrise
unique: The first place in the United States to catch the sunrise for much of the year: you drive a granite dome above the Atlantic fog and watch the light hit Frenchman Bay.
buzz: Rangers and repeat visitors all say the same thing, go on a clear morning, arrive 45 minutes early, and bring more layers than you think. The reservation system is the only complaint.

name: Katahdin via the Knife Edge
unique: The terminus of the Appalachian Trail and the only real above-treeline ridge in the Northeast: a mile of knife edge granite with thousand foot drops on both sides.
buzz: Hikers call it the best day hike east of the Rockies and warn, correctly, that the Knife Edge is a bad first mountain. Weather turns fast; rangers turn people around.

name: Haystack Mountain School of Crafts
unique: A modernist campus on a granite ledge over the Atlantic, where intensive craft workshops run for decades and the architecture is as memorable as the classes.
buzz: People call it a pilgrimage; the location is remote and the schedule is intense. Scholarships exist and are worth asking about.

name: Coastal Maine Botanical Gardens
unique: Three hundred acres of gardens on a tidal saltwater frontage, with five huge wooden trolls hidden in the woods, a children's garden and a rhododendron trail.
buzz: The trolls are why families come and the gardens are why gardeners return; allow three hours and wear walking shoes.

name: Schooner Sail on Penobscot Bay
unique: You haul lines on a restored coastal schooner among the same pine islands and puffin ledges that carried lime, ice and granite for a century. No engine, no narration track.
buzz: Crews are praised for actually letting guests steer and haul; seasickness is rare in the bay. Book the sunset sail over midday if you only do one.

name: Camden Hills State Park
company: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands
unique: A ridge of granite hills above Camden harbor, with trails to Mount Battie and a view of Penobscot Bay and the islands.
buzz: The Mount Battie road is the easy view and the ridge trail is the real hike; the park is popular in October.

name: Common Ground Country Fair
company: Maine Organic Farmers and Gardeners Association
unique: A state fair rebuilt around draft horses, oxen, heirloom seeds and woodlot skills, fried dough exists, but so does a working cider press and a sheepdog trial.
buzz: People describe it as the anti-state-fair: earnest, enormous, and genuinely useful. Parking and the Saturday crowd are the recurring gripes.

name: Kennebec River Rafting
customer: Groups, families with teens, adventure seekers
unique: Class IV and V whitewater on a dam controlled river, with a 12 foot drop at Magic Falls and a calmer float below for the second half.
buzz: Outfitters say the autumn release weekends are the biggest water; the river is cold and the trip runs rain or shine.

name: Maine Maritime Museum
unique: A shipyard museum on the Kennebec where a 19th century shipbuilding yard is preserved, with a working wooden boat shop and cruises on the river.
buzz: The boat shop and the yard are the real thing and the river cruise is the add on; children like the lobstering exhibit.

name: Ocean Path
unique: A flat two mile path along the granite cliffs of Acadia from Sand Beach to Otter Point, passing Thunder Hole and the pink granite ledges.
buzz: Thunder Hole is the crowded stop and Otter Cliff is the photograph; the path is easy and the waves at high tide are the show.

name: Sugarloaf
unique: The largest ski area in the east by vertical, with above treeline terrain, a snowfields bowl and a drive that ends in the middle of nowhere.
buzz: Skiers come for the steeps and the lack of crowds midweek; the access road is long and the wind holds lifts.

name: Lobster Boat and Trap Haul
unique: A working lobsterman pulls traps, bands a keeper, and explains the fishery in the same breath, then you eat a lobster on the dock that was in the water that morning.
buzz: The good operators are loved for blunt humor and genuine knowledge; the bad ones are floating gift shops. Ask whether the boat is actually hauling gear before you book.

name: Colby College Museum of Art
unique: A college museum with the Alex Katz collection, a Whistler room and a wing by Frederick Fisher, free and better than most city museums of its size.
buzz: Art people make the drive from Portland for the Katz and the American galleries; the museum is free and the campus is walkable.

name: Cutler Coast
company: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands
unique: A bold coast of volcanic headlands and spruce forest where the trail runs along the cliff edge to coves you can only reach on foot.
buzz: The bold coast loop is the best coastal hike in the state and the fog is part of it; the trail is rough and the parking is a small lot on a dirt road.

name: Moosehead Lake
unique: The largest lake in Maine, 40 miles long, ringed by unbroken forest where moose come down to the road at dusk and the steamboat Katahdin still runs.
buzz: The drive along the eastern shore at dusk is the moose route; fly fishing for brook trout and the float plane rides are the local specialties.

name: Portland Head Light
unique: Washington's first lighthouse, on a headland above the entrance to Portland harbor, with the keeper's house and a park of gun emplacements around it.
buzz: The park is free and the view of the lighthouse from the beach below is the photograph; the museum in the keeper's house is small.

name: Sunday River
unique: Eight connected peaks with a lift system that spreads crowds, wide groomers and a resort base that makes a week easy without a car.
buzz: Families like the variety and the snowmaking; experts prefer Sugarloaf and the base area is a long walk from some lodging.

name: Grafton Notch State Park
company: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands
unique: A mountain pass with a gorge of potholes and waterfalls, a short trail to Screw Auger Falls and the trailheads for Old Speck and the Mahoosucs.
buzz: The falls are a five minute walk and the Table Rock trail is the view; the park is quiet compared with Acadia.

name: Maine Huts and Trails
unique: A chain of off grid lodges connected by 80 miles of trail through the Carrabassett valley, with bunk rooms, wood heat and meals cooked by a hutmaster.
buzz: People ski hut to hut in winter and hike in summer; the huts are comfortable and the booking system fills months ahead.

name: Marginal Way
unique: A mile and a quarter of paved footpath along the top of the sea wall between Ogunquit beach and Perkins Cove, with granite benches and rose bushes.
buzz: It is the most walkable mile on the Maine coast and busy on summer mornings; the cove at the south end has the lobster shack.

name: Popham Beach State Park
company: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands
unique: A sand spit that shifts with the tide, with a view of two islands and the remains of Fort Popham at one end, near the site of the 1607 Popham colony.
buzz: At low tide you can walk to Fox Island and the currents at the river mouth are dangerous; the beach is wide and rarely packed.

name: Fort Knox
company: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands
unique: A granite fort on the Penobscot with casemates, a dry moat and a view of the Penobscot Narrows Bridge, never finished and never fired a shot in anger.
buzz: The fort is dark and open to roam and children love it; the bridge observatory next door is the add on.

name: Lily Bay State Park
company: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands
unique: A sandy beach and campground on the east shore of Moosehead Lake, with a view of Katahdin across the water and canoe rentals at the dock.
buzz: The beach is the best on the lake and the campground books early; the water is cold and the sunsets are the reason to stay.

name: Machias Wild Blueberry Festival
unique: A church run festival in the blueberry capital of the world, with a pie eating contest, a blueberry pancake breakfast and a parade through a town of 2,000.
buzz: The pies and the breakfast are the reason to come; it is small, genuine and the drive is long enough to keep it that way.

name: Maine Mineral and Gem Museum
unique: A world class mineral collection in a Bethel storefront, including the largest meteorite found in the state and a walk in gem vault.
buzz: Rockhounds call it a hidden gem and the fluorescent mineral room is the surprise; children like the gold panning.

name: Maine Potato Blossom Festival
unique: A week of potato themed events in the county that grows most of the country's potatoes, with a parade, a mash potato wrestling match and fields of blossoms in July.
buzz: The parade and the food stands are the tradition; it is a real county fair atmosphere with almost no tourists.

name: Maine State Prison Store
unique: A store selling furniture, toys and chess sets made by inmates in the prison workshop next door, with a sign in sheet and no photos allowed.
buzz: The craftsmanship is excellent and the prices are low; staff are matter of fact about where the work comes from. A strange and worthwhile stop.

name: Pemaquid Point Lighthouse
unique: A lighthouse on a point of folded rock ledges where the surf runs up the strata, with a fisherman's museum in the keeper's house.
buzz: The rock ledges are the photograph and the museum is small; it is on the Maine quarter and the sunrise is the local ritual.

name: Portland Museum of Art
unique: A museum with the Winslow Homer studio collection, a Pei wing and a strong Maine painting collection, in a downtown block a few steps from the water.
buzz: The Homer galleries are the reason to come and the Wyeths are the local favorite; the free Friday evening is packed.

name: Rangeley Lake
unique: A deep cold lake in the western mountains with landlocked salmon and brook trout, ringed by public land and a small resort town.
buzz: Fishermen come for the salmon in spring and the fall color is the other season; the lake is big and the wind picks up.

name: Acadian Village
unique: A collection of 19th century Acadian houses and barns moved to a site on the St. John River, with guides who speak the French of the upper valley.
buzz: Visitors from Louisiana and France come for the genealogy; the village is quiet and the river view is the setting.

name: Boothbay Railway Village
unique: A village of moved and restored buildings around a narrow gauge steam railroad, with a Model T ride and a collection of antique automobiles.
buzz: The steam train ride is short and the village is the charm; good with children under ten and quiet in September.

name: Katahdin Cruises
unique: The SS Katahdin, a 1914 steamboat still running on Moosehead Lake, with a route past islands and a view of Katahdin from the water.
buzz: The boat is the attraction and the crew points out moose on the shore; the afternoon trip is the quieter one.

name: Nubble Lighthouse
unique: A lighthouse on a rocky island just offshore, connected to the mainland by nothing, with a keeper's house and a view of Cape Neddick.
buzz: The classic photo is from Sohier Park at sunset and the island is not open to the public; parking is limited in summer.

name: Old Fort Western
customer: History families, rev war people, school groups
unique: The oldest surviving wooden fort in New England, a storehouse and garrison on the Kennebec built for the French and Indian War, with the original timbers.
buzz: The guides are in period dress and the storehouse is the best building; it is small and the river setting is the rest.

name: Basilica of Saints Peter and Paul
unique: A granite French Gothic church with a 160 foot tower and rose windows, built by French Canadian mill workers in a mill town.
buzz: The scale is a surprise in a small city and it is free to look; it is an active parish, so avoid Mass times.

name: Belfast Harbor
unique: A working waterfront with a footbridge, a farmers market, a boatyard and a rail trail along the bay, in a town that rebuilt itself around its harbor.
buzz: The coop and the harbor walk are the local ritual; the town is quieter than Camden and the sailing school takes beginners.

name: Cole Land Transportation Museum
unique: A hangar of Maine snowplows, logging trucks, fire engines and a 1920s bus, put together by a truck dealer who bought back the state's working vehicles.
buzz: The snowplow and logging equipment are the local history; the military hall next door is separate and free.

name: Hudson Museum
unique: A university anthropology museum with a strong Wabanaki collection, birchbark canoes and baskets, free and open to the public.
buzz: The Wabanaki baskets and the Penobscot canoe are the highlights; it is small and the staff are helpful.

name: Kennebec River Rail Trail
unique: A paved trail along the Kennebec from Gardiner to Augusta, past shipyards, a paper mill and the river where the state's shipbuilding began.
buzz: The Bath waterfront and the river views are the reason to ride; the trail is flat and connects to downtown Bath.

name: Mount Hope Cemetery
customer: History walkers, Stephen King readers, photographers
unique: A Victorian garden cemetery on a hill above Bangor where Hannibal Hamlin is buried and the gates and stone chapels appear in Stephen King's fiction.
buzz: King readers come for the locations and historians come for the Civil War generals; the self guided map is at the gate.

name: Museum L-A
customer: Labor history people, local families, students
unique: A museum in a former shoe shop telling the story of the mills that drew French Canadian, Greek and Somali workers to Lewiston, with the machines still threaded.
buzz: The oral histories are the exhibit and the volunteers are often former mill workers; it is small and personal.

name: Lost Valley
unique: A community ski hill with night skiing, a tiny vertical and a lodge that has not changed much since the 1960s, 30 minutes from Portland.
buzz: Locals learn here and the night sessions are cheap; experts will be bored in an hour.

name: Maine State House
unique: A granite capitol designed with Charles Bulfinch, with a copper dome and a hall of flags, in a city that exists mainly to be the capital.
buzz: The dome and the chambers are the quick tour and it is free; the Maine State Museum next door is the bigger visit.

name: Nylander Museum
unique: A small museum built around the collection of a Swedish immigrant self taught naturalist, with fossils, shells and Aroostook County farm history.
buzz: The collection is old fashioned and charming and the volunteers know the county; it takes an hour.
